notes: 2026-10-30 review fail by reviewer: FAIL, two security defects. (1) apps/web/next.config.ts:35: Next matches header sources without case (routes-manifest caseSensitive false), so (?!embed/) also skips /EMBED/ and /Embed/. The proxy matcher (src/proxy.ts:35) and the app routes are case-sensitive. Result: /EMBED/<anything> answers the 404 page with no CSP and no X-Frame-Options. Reproduced on the verified build with curl. In Chromium a page on another origin framed it, and a click on Back to Forwend soft-navigated the frame to / (landing h1 rendered inside the foreign frame). Control /embedX/... was refused. Before this change every response had frame-ancestors 'none' and DENY. Fix: make the skip and the proxy agree, for example keep FRAME_HEADERS on every path and let the proxy replace them on /embed/<token> (a probe showed the proxy's CSP replaces the config one), or make the proxy send 'none' for every path except an exact /embed/<token>. Add /EMBED/<token> to the header test (e2e/pay.spec.ts:1199). (2) apps/backend/internal/profile/stores.go:73-88: origin() takes any host url.Parse takes, including *, *.example.com, a.com;sandbox, a.com'x and a.com,b.com. A store can save https://*. FramedBy (stores.go:66) then allows origin=https://* because it equals the stored value, and the proxy sends frame-ancestors https://*: any https site can frame that store's checkout. So the exact-origin rule (accept 2, D-117, FramedBy doc, openapi) is not enforced. No whitespace gets through, so no other directive value can be injected. Fix: accept only a hostname (letters, digits, hyphen, dot) or 127.0.0.1 plus a numeric port, and add https://* and https://*.example.com rejection cases to stores_test.go. Non-blocking: page.tsx:19 reads a repeated origin param as empty while proxy.ts:13 checks the first value; postMessage('') then throws (nothing leaks), and the status post in use-embed-messages.ts:28 would throw inside an effect. No ready is posted when the invoice fails to load. new-invoice-form.tsx:559 and invoices-copy.ts:147 list http://localhost origins as return-link starts, but return links stay https only (invoice.go:488). docs/web/architecture.md PayScreen bullet is 26 words. Checked and fine: proxy fails closed on a bad token, missing API_URL, backend down or timeout, non-200, bad JSON. A third party cannot inject into the CSP. /embed/<token> sends one CSP and no XFO. /, /app, /pay and bare /embed keep 'none' and DENY. postMessage never goes to *, only to the origin the CSP allowed, and the embed has no message listener. Live invoices are https only. Return links are still https only. The hook posts ready once, status only after ready, and cancels rAF and the observer on cleanup (StrictMode safe). Leaving links open _blank or _top, and PDFs are attachment downloads. The theme script takes only a THEMES value. Docker runtime API_URL is read at run time. The Go embed test passes (ran it). The refused-frame and header e2e tests would fail without the protection, and they fit Which tests to keep. No fixed waits. Structure and dependency direction are fine.

notes: 2026-10-31 review fail by reviewer: FAIL on acceptance 3: the provenance publish workflow cannot work as written, and it claims an approval gate that does not exist. (1) None of the packages it offers has a repository field (packages/js/package.json, packages/react/package.json, packages/node/package.json). The npm registry rejects a provenance publish unless package.json repository.url matches the GitHub repo, so .github/workflows/publish.yml:42 fails for all three. Add repository {type git, url git+https://github.com/Forwend/forwend.git, directory packages/<name>} and make scripts/check-browser-packages.mjs assert it. (2) Forwend/forwend is PRIVATE and the org plan is free (checked with gh). npm makes provenance only from public repositories. GitHub offers environments and required reviewers on a free-plan private repo only with Enterprise, and the repo has no environments today. A job that names a missing environment gets one created with no rules. So publish.yml:3-4 ('the npm environment's required reviewers approve it first'), packages/js/AGENTS.md:10, packages/react/AGENTS.md:10 and proof line 3 state a gate and provenance that cannot exist yet. Today nothing can publish only because no NPM_TOKEN secret exists. State the real prerequisites: a public repo, an npm environment with required reviewers and main-only deployment, and NPM_TOKEN as an npm environment secret only. Or record them as an owner decision; do not claim the gate exists. Everything else is fine. Security: messages.ts:45-49 accepts only event.source === iframe.contentWindow, the exact baseUrl origin, source forwend, v 1 and typed fields. Removing the source check, or removeEventListener in destroy, made the js and React tests fail; I tried both on a scratch copy. payToken is checked against /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/ before any /embed or /pay URL, the same pattern as apps/web PAY_TOKEN_PATTERN. The origin param is window.location.origin, as proxy.ts and EMBED_PARAMS expect. The package holds no key, and events are hints only. React: StrictMode keeps one frame, and a new handler runs without a remount. Unmount clears the listener, timer and frame. dist/checkout.js keeps 'use client', and SSR renders an empty div. pnpm --filter @forwend/react-18-check test: 5 passed on React 18, including the version assert; dedupe makes the source and tests load react 18.3.1. In a scratch app, the packed tarballs with react 18.3.1 and @types/react 18.3.12 passed tsc and SSR. node scripts/check-browser-packages.mjs exits 0, at 2237/3072 B and 1084/2048 B gzip. The packed react manifest depends on @forwend/js ^0.1.0. A mutated copy exits 1 on an over-budget size and on a type error. The lockfile diff adds only the new importers and React 18. The config check and path rule are correct. Kept tests guard trust boundaries and cleanup, and none are timing-dependent. Non-blocking: (a) linkUrl (checkout.ts:65-67) takes any slug, and '..' resolves to https://forwend.com/. Real slugs match /^[a-z0-9]{12}$/ (apps/web/src/features/links/constants/links.ts:29). Validate slugs the same way and replace the never-valid 'spring-sale' in tests, smoke and README. It is a link only, never framed. (b) pay-button.tsx:11 turns payToken='' into href /l/ instead of throwing. (c) check-browser-packages.mjs:27-28,137 pipe stdout and keep only the first error line, so tsc errors are hidden. The temp dir is also not removed on SIGINT. (d) In js README:18, getElementById returns HTMLElement|null, so the example fails strict TS. (e) publish.yml:38 does not run the React 18 tests before publishing @forwend/react. (f) docs/tasks.json also carries the unrelated F413 entry; ship it separately or say so in the PR.

tasks.behavior: Payments confirm and settle without waiting for unrelated offered networks
acceptance: Reproduce: a payment final on its own network stays unbooked while another offered network lags. Keep a regression test.
The first payment final on its own network chooses its option, is booked and queued to settle at once; no other offered network is waited for.

Safety holds: only final deposits of the invoice's own token count, zero-value transfers are ignored, the paid balance is checked at the finalized block before settling, one option wins under the invoice lock, and money on any other option is held for the payer.
R-56, R-119, D-76 and the backend docs describe the rule; no new screen text.
notes: 2026-10-30 Owner request: investigate and fix cross-network waiting, then let the implementing agent merge. This task records findings only; no implementation is started.

2026-10-30 Root cause: internal/ledger/process.go:100-126 refuses to choose an option until every other enabled option chain has last_finalized_time greater than the deposit block_time. It returns before booking; settlement_intents are created only after paid at lines 336-343. The slowest offered network therefore delays faster ones.

2026-10-30 Current policy deliberately chooses the earliest payment across chains (R-119/D-76), protecting an earlier full payment from later dust. This is a policy change, not permission to delete the guard or replace finalized evidence with latest blocks. Preserve the safety purpose through an explicit attempt-selection design.

2026-10-30 internal/invoice/pick.go:16-18 currently treats the payer pick as display preference, not binding payment selection. internal/invoice/payments.go:61 labels detected as Confirming even when the deposit itself is confirmed and only cross-network selection is waiting.

2026-10-30 Measured local database evidence, 2026-10-30 UTC: Tempo 0x5eaa56eea0b52674330f56160a4ee4021075291def5446ccb5e2c134bb4009df detected in 9.4s, waited 1080.7s until settlement queued, then signed in 9.2s and settled in 12.1s from queue. Tempo 0x4735a3cc5987f8d264af525219ac6bdc5a3447eabfbe03597692f785f79f9448 detected in 3.8s, waited 1351.6s, then signed in 7.2s and settled in 10.0s from queue. The dominant delay was before signing.

2026-10-30 Live Arc reproduction: payment option 0x0db52f3af21065f01e04d2f76b37a6f93aca52e9d6a7c8ea1fd8bbb5b5616121 deposited at 23:13:08 UTC, transfer confirmed but booked=false and chosen_id NULL. Tempo/Arc finalized through 23:15:17/23:15:16; Base/Arbitrum only through 22:56:50/22:54:44. Both unused rollups blocked selection. No settlement intent existed.

2026-10-30 Reproduction recipe: create a multi-network payment, keep Base or Arbitrum finalized cursor behind a fully finalized Tempo/Arc deposit, run ledger processing, and inspect booked, chosen_id and settlement_intents. Advance only the unrelated cursor and observe the current implementation finally queue settlement. Extend existing internal/ledger/options_test.go coverage; use disposable data.

2026-10-30 Scope and limits: user reports local and staging. Local SQL/history and running logs were inspected; origin/staging had the same guard, but staging runtime data was not accessed. Local worker/signer poll every 30s; Arc Blockdaemon also returned invalid responses. These are secondary observations, not the proven cause of the 18-22 minute selection waits.

2026-10-30 Acceptance must cover reloads, competing browser tabs, selection changes before detection, deposits discovered after switching, chain outages and legacy multi-option invoices. Do not trust a mutable browser pick to redirect or discard existing money. Existing receiver addresses and signed terms remain valid.

tasks.behavior: A deposit below 1 USD never decides which option a payer-chooses invoice takes
acceptance: A final deposit below the minimum (1 USD, or the invoice amount if smaller) never chooses an option; the first payment at or above it, on any option, is chosen.
Money below the minimum stays held for the payer and stays refundable; it never blocks the invoice from expiring or from settling the chosen option.
Payer and owner pages show it as money held for the payer, never as a partial payment of an option nobody chose.
Tests: dust on one network before a full payment on another; a real partial payment then a top-up; dust only, then expiry.
R-56, R-119 and D-90 state the minimum, and PLAN's open dust-threshold item is closed.
